summary: Extend the accepted classical rigidity plan by the filtered integral Taylor comparison of GSWZ §5.1. The naive completion is imported from HC.1–HC.2. Universal cyclotomic coefficient algebras, multiplicative Taylor coordinates, finite matrices, corrected determinant indexing and the integral image criterion are specified for torsion-free coefficient rings. Finite integral-extension separatedness repairs the coefficient-change boundary in the inherited rootwise rigidity proof.

nodes.title: The untwisted universal Taylor product
nodes.statement: Write A_m(R)=R[q]/(Phi_m(q))=R tensor_Z Z[zeta_m], with universal root z_m. Define TaylorProduct R = product over m>=1 of A_m(R)[[u]], where q=z_m(1-u). Coefficients C_{m,l} have exponent l-1. This is the tensor-product coefficient algebra, even when a chosen root already lies in R: it retains every cyclotomic component. Its reduced representative gives gamma_{m,l,j} in R for 0<=j<phi(m). For R=Z it is the usual product of Z[zeta_m][[u]]. No choice of an embedded compositum replaces A_m for arbitrary R.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Use the baseline AdjoinRoot quotient and its monic power basis; its rank is phi(m) by natDegree_cyclotomic.
Take the product of power-series R-algebras; define coordinates by coefficients followed by the canonical reduced representative.
For a chosen embedded root, liftAlgHom specializes A_m(R) to R[zeta]; the specialization can have a kernel, and is not the product definition.

Coefficients C_{m,l} have exponent l-1. This is the tensor-product coefficient algebra, even when a chosen root already lies in R: it retains every cyclotomic component. Its reduced representative gives gamma_{m,l,j} in R for 0<=j<phi(m). For R=Z it is the usual product of Z[zeta_m][[u]]. No choice of an embedded compositum replaces A_m for arbitrary R.

nodes.title: The factorial kernel filtration
nodes.statement: For H_R=R[q]^(positive orders), imported by factorial cofinality, define hFiltration R N=kernel(H_R->R[q]/(P_{N-1})), where P_n=product_{i=1}^n(1-q^i), N>=1. It equals P_{N-1}H_R and consists of normalized expansions with a_{n,k}=0 for n<N in the GSWZ indexing 1<=n,0<=k<n. Thus hFiltration R 1=H_R, the ideals decrease with N, and their intersection is zero.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Use HC.1 finite quotient kernels with the factorial cofinal system.
Translate HC.2 digits a_{n-1} into GSWZ a_n; the first N-1 digits vanish exactly when the projection vanishes.
Separatedness follows from extensionality on all factorial quotients.

nodes.title: The weighted Taylor filtration
nodes.statement: Define pFiltration R N as the ideal of f in TaylorProduct R with C_{m,l}(f)=0 whenever m*l<N. Equivalently f_m is divisible by u^floor((N-1)/m). The quotient retains exactly the coordinates with m*l<N. The filtration decreases, starts at the whole product for N=1, and has zero intersection. Multiplication preserves each ideal because vanishing below a fixed power of u is a componentwise ideal condition.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Use the coefficientwise power-series ideal u^floor((N-1)/m).
A coefficient with exponent k is retained precisely when m*(k+1)<N; show floor((N-1)/m)=ceil(N/m)-1 for m>0.
Every fixed coordinate is eventually retained, giving separatedness.

nodes.title: Factorial projection kernels and separation
nodes.statement: For N>=1, the kernel of H_R->R[q]/P_(N-1) is the principal ideal P_(N-1)H_R; equivalently its first N-1 normalized digits vanish. These kernels decrease, their intersection is zero, and the projection induces H_R/kernel ≅ R[q]/P_(N-1).
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Apply the imported finite completion quotient theorem at P_(N-1).
The unique factorial digits show that the kernel consists precisely of the factorial tail, whose factor P_(N-1) may be taken out coefficientwise.
The compatible-family description proves the decreasing and zero-intersection assertions.
acceptance: At N=1 the kernel is the whole ring; at N=2 the polynomial kernel is evaluation at 1.

nodes.title: The factorial graded piece
nodes.statement: For N>=1, the R-linear map [g] -> [P_{N-1}g] identifies R[q]/(1-q^N) with hFiltration R N / hFiltration R (N+1). Both sides are free of rank N. Quotients of nested ideals here are quotients of R-submodules. No claim that this is a unital ring isomorphism is made.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Use the imported unique factorial expansion: its Nth digit has degree <N.
Multiplication by the polynomial P_{N-1}, whose leading coefficient is a unit, identifies the leading digit modulo 1-q^N; cancellation proves the stated kernel.

nodes.title: Finite precision bases and ranks
nodes.statement: H_R/hFiltration R N has the R-basis q^k P_{n-1} for 1<=n<N, 0<=k<n. TaylorProduct R/pFiltration R N has the R-basis z_m^j u^(l-1), supported at component m, for m*l<N and 0<=j<phi(m). Their common number of basis elements is d_N=N(N-1)/2, and both inverse systems recover their infinite objects. These are finite-level basis and base-change statements; an infinite product is not an algebraic tensor product in general.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Apply the two graded-piece results successively using the digit and coefficient splittings already constructed.
Count sum_{1<=n<N} n using Nat.sum_totient for the Taylor side.
Inverse-limit reconstruction follows by digit/coefficient extensionality; finite free modules allow ordinary coefficient base change at each N.
acceptance: N=1 has dimension 0, N=3 has dimension 3, N=5 has dimension 10.

nodes.title: The multiplicative Taylor comparison
nodes.statement: Define iota : H_R ->_R TaylorProduct R by expanding q=z_m(1-u) in the universal algebra A_m(R) for every positive m. Its coefficient of u^k on a polynomial g is (-z_m)^k times the kth Hasse derivative of g at z_m. It is the HC.3 Taylor map followed by x=-z_m u, a zero-constant-term linear change of variable. This is ordinary untwisted completion, and does not define GSWZ Definition 1.1.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Use HC.3/the-taylor-map with A_m(R), where Phi_m(z_m)=0 by the quotient relation.
Apply the variable scaling x=-z_m u; on polynomials it is evaluation at z_m(1-u), and coefficientwise multiplication shows the ring laws.
Take the product over m.

nodes.title: Vanishing orders of factorial products
nodes.statement: For n>=0 and m>=1, in A_m(R)[u], P_n(z_m(1-u)) is divisible by u^floor(n/m). Consequently iota(hFiltration R N) is contained in pFiltration R N. Over a torsion-free R the leading coefficient calculated below is nonzero when n=m*l-1, but exact order is not asserted over arbitrary R.

proofSteps: Separate the factors with index divisible by m: each has zero constant term, since z_m^m=1.
There are floor(n/m) such factors; multiply their u divisibility.
Use the principal-kernel characterization and the algebra-map property of iota: multiplying the Taylor collection of P_(N-1) by another collection preserves these coefficient-vanishing ideals.

nodes.statement: In A_m(Z) for m>=1, product_{r=1}^{m-1}(1-z_m^r)=m. The same identity holds after any coefficient change. For m=1 both sides are 1. It is proved in the universal integral cyclotomic quotient, not by cancellation over an arbitrary R.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: The monic-remainder basis embeds A_m(Z) in A_m(Q). Polynomial.cyclotomic_eq_minpoly_rat and minpoly.dvd_iff embed A_m(Q) in a characteristic-zero cyclotomic field by evaluation at a primitive root.
Apply the existing domain identity IsPrimitiveRoot.prod_one_sub_pow_eq_order in that field, with n=m-1 in its successor indexing, and transfer back by the injective embedding.
Use the quotient universal property for arbitrary R.

nodes.title: Leading Taylor coefficient of a factorial product
nodes.statement: For m,l>=1, the coefficients below exponent l-1 of P_{ml-1}(z_m(1-u)) vanish and its coefficient at l-1 equals D_{m,l}. Thus P_{ml-1}(z_m(1-u))=D_{m,l}u^(l-1) modulo u^l in A_m(R)[u].
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: For each multiple i=m*j, j=1,...,l-1, the factor 1-(1-u)^i starts with m*j*u.
For each nonzero residue r mod m there are l indices <=m*l-1; the product of their constant terms is (product_{r=1}^{m-1}(1-z_m^r))^l=m^l.
Multiply the two contributions: m^(l-1)*(l-1)! times m^l.
acceptance: P_3 at q=-(1-u) has coefficient of u equal to 8; P_3 at q=1-u starts with 6u^3.

nodes.title: The graded Taylor map
nodes.statement: Under the two graded-piece equivalences, gr_N(iota) sends [g] in R[q]/(1-q^N) to (D_{m,N/m}*g(z_m))_{m|N}. The order is N in both filtrations. No derivative of g enters this first surviving coefficient.

proofSteps: Multiply g(z_m(1-u)) by the leading coefficient of P_{N-1} at m|N.
Only g(z_m) contributes to exponent N/m-1; use factorial-leading-coefficient.

nodes.title: Simultaneous cyclotomic remainders are injective
nodes.statement: For torsion-free R, the remainder map E_N:R[q]/(q^N-1)->product_{m|N} A_m(R) is injective. For a Q-algebra R it is an isomorphism. For arbitrary torsion-free R no integral Chinese-remainder surjectivity is claimed.
hypotheses: R is torsion-free as an abelian group; no domain or Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Over Q, distinct cyclotomic polynomials are coprime; their product is q^N-1, so CRT is an isomorphism.
Use monic reduced representatives to identify the integral map with a square integer matrix; it has nonzero determinant because its Q extension is an isomorphism.
Apply its adjugate to a kernel vector. A nonzero integer acts injectively on the underlying Z-module R, so the vector is zero.
acceptance: At N=2, E_2(a+bq)=(a+b,a-b), whose integral cokernel has order 2.

nodes.title: The integral finite Taylor matrix
nodes.statement: Define taylorMatrix N=M_N, a square integer matrix of size d_N=N(N-1)/2. Columns are (n,k) ordered by increasing n, then k, with 1<=n<N,0<=k<n. Rows are (m,l,j) ordered by increasing weight m*l, decreasing m within a weight, then increasing j, with m*l<N,0<=j<phi(m). Entry ((m,l,j),(n,k)) is coefficient j of the reduced cyclotomic representative of the coefficient u^(l-1) in z_m^k(1-u)^k P_{n-1}(z_m(1-u)). The matrix over R is entrywise integer casting. All row/column order choices are pinned.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Enumerate the finite bases from finite-precision-bases using the displayed order.
Compute each entry by integral Hasse coefficients and reduction modulo the monic Phi_m in Z[z_m].
For arbitrary R monic reduction commutes with coefficient change; the universal algebra keeps the basis rank phi(m).

nodes.title: Determinant of a two-factor remainder map
nodes.statement: For monic f,g in Z[q], the square integral map Z[q]/(fg)->Z[q]/(f) direct-sum Z[q]/(g), in monomial quotient bases, has absolute determinant equal to |Res(f,g)|. This does not require integral comaximality.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; positive precision N and positive root order m. Rank assertions assume R is nontrivial. Torsion-freeness over Z is imposed only on the injectivity and image statements that use it.
proofSteps: Change the source basis to 1,q,...,q^(deg f-1), f,qf,...,q^(deg g-1) by a unit triangular matrix.
The remainder matrix becomes block triangular: identity on the f quotient and multiplication by f on the g quotient.

Apply monic division by g to the target coefficient space of the Sylvester map (a,b)->g*a+f*b. The new basis 1,q,...,q^(deg g-1),g,qg,...,q^(deg f-1) is unit triangular. The coefficient matrix has multiplication by f modulo g and an identity diagonal block. Polynomial.toMatrix_sylvesterMap and the definition of resultant identify its determinant up to permutation sign. This avoids a separability or integral CRT assumption.

nodes.title: Scalar divisibility in an integer localization
nodes.statement: Let Delta be a nonzero integer, d a positive integer, and a in R=Z[1/Delta]. Then a belongs to dR iff, for every prime p not dividing Delta, its canonical image in Z_p belongs to dZ_p. The map R->Z_p is defined because Delta is a unit there. The zero scalar a is handled separately from finite valuation formulas.

proofSteps: Write a=b/Delta^k using the localization fraction representation. For p not dividing Delta, the denominator is a p-adic unit by the integer norm criterion; extend the integer map by localization universality.
Use PadicInt.unitCoeff_spec to replace the nonzero integer d by p^v_p(d) up to a p-adic unit. Thus local divisibility is the inequality v_p(a)>=v_p(d).

Use Padic.valuation_ratCast and padicValRat.defn to compute v_p(a)=v_p(b) outside Delta. Nat.factorization_le_iff_dvd shows that the prime-to-Delta factor of d divides b exactly when all these inequalities hold. The remaining factors of d are units in R.
For a=0 both global and local divisibility hold directly.

nodes.statement: Let R and B be domains, with an injective ring map R->B and B finite as an R-module. There exist r>=1 and an injective R-linear map B->R^r. No freeness, normality, or Noetherian hypothesis on B or R is imposed.
hypotheses: R and B are domains; R->B is injective and B is a finite R-module.
proofSteps: Choose finitely many R-module generators of B using Module.Finite.exists_fin. Embed Frac(R) into Frac(B) by injectivity and let V be their finite-dimensional Frac(R)-linear span.
Choose a basis of V. Each generator has finitely many fraction-field coordinates; choose one common nonzero d in R clearing all their denominators.

For b in B define its coordinates in that basis and multiply each coordinate by d. Since the generators have coordinates in R after this multiplication, every b does. This gives an R-linear map B->R^r.
The map is injective because the fraction-field embedding, basis-coordinate map and multiplication by d are injective. Nontriviality of B makes the dimension positive.
acceptance: R[zeta_m] is a finite domain extension in an algebraic closure of Frac(R); this lemma applies even when it is not free over R.

nodes.title: Adic separation transfers to a finite domain extension
nodes.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, for c in R, if intersection_{k>=0} c^k R=0 then intersection_{k>=0} c^k B=0. In particular p-adic separatedness of R transfers to the actual embedded ring R[zeta_m] for every prime p. This closes the non-Noetherian transfer boundary of the imported Theorem 5.2 proof.
hypotheses: R->B is an injective finite extension of domains; c-adic separatedness is assumed for R.
proofSteps: Apply the injective R-linear map B->R^r. If b belongs to c^k B for every k, each coordinate of its image belongs to c^k R for every k.
R-separatedness kills each coordinate; injectivity kills b.
R[zeta_m] is generated by 1,zeta_m,...,zeta_m^(phi(m)-1) because the cyclotomic polynomial is monic.
acceptance: The inherited rootwise Taylor theorem needs no extra Noetherian hypothesis to transfer its prime-separation assumptions to R[zeta]. This lemma does not claim separation for an infinite union of cyclotomic extensions.

restructure.detail: The atlas HC.4 description omits the accepted PLAN-HABIRO/RS-10 assignment of the naive filtered Taylor comparison and still has an ambiguous general evaluation-at-individual-roots boundary.
restructure.proposal: Add GSWZ §5.1 to HC.4 with universal tensor-product cyclotomic coefficient algebras and corrected precision indexing. Keep Theorem 6.1 and the accepted irreducible-cyclotomic special case of Theorem 6.2. Do not enlarge the target to evaluation at arbitrary incomplete sets of conjugate roots over arbitrary subrings of Qbar: no atlas consumer requests it and the parent packet records an unresolved proof boundary. The finite-domain separation-transfer lemma supplies the non-Noetherian input to Theorem 5.2 without editing the parent packet.

restructure.title: Separate classical rigidity from the finite integral comparison
restructure.detail: The accepted parent HC.4 carries five classical-rigidity planets; the integral comparison adds six central objects and theorems. A combined stage would obscure the two proof chains and exceed six displayed planets.
restructure.proposal: On assembly split HC.4 into Classical arithmetic rigidity (HC.4a) and Integral Taylor comparison (HC.4b). HC.4a contains the fifteen imported parent HC.4 nodes plus the two finite-domain transfer lemmas and retains its five planets. HC.4b contains the thirty-four integral-comparison nodes of this part and its six planets. Both use HC.1–HC.3; HC.4b imports the resultant lemma from HC.4a and the existing HC.5 rational/prime-inversion decomposition. Maintain the current HC.4 identifiers as declaration aliases and redirect HB.6 finite-matrix consumption to HC.4b. The finite-domain embedding and separation-transfer nodes in this part belong in HC.4a and are used by rootwise-taylor-injectivity; they carry no additional planet.
